questions.q: Sort each statement by the kind of software licence it describes.
items: The source code is published and can be changed
The source code is kept secret by the company
Usually free to download and use
Normally comes with paid support from the company
Anyone may distribute a modified version
Changing or redistributing it is forbidden by the licence
questions.feedback: The licence is the difference, not the price. There is paid open source software and free proprietary software.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 7 — Licence lab, station 3: Open source software

questions.q: A charity is choosing between open source and proprietary office software. Explain one advantage of each.

markPoints.concept: open source is usually free, which matters to a charity
accept: free|no cost|costs nothing|no licence fee|no fee|cheaper|saves money
markPoints.exemplar: Open source is usually free, which matters when money is tight.

markPoints.concept: and it can be changed to suit the charity's own needs
markPoints.exemplar: Its source code can be changed to suit their own needs.

markPoints.concept: proprietary software normally comes with support from the company
accept: support|help|helpdesk|technical support|customer service|company behind it|someone to call|someone to ask|to call when|guarantee|warranty
markPoints.exemplar: Proprietary software comes with support from the company.

markPoints.concept: and is usually better tested and more widely compatible
accept: better tested|well tested|thoroughly tested|tested properly|reliable|stable|polished|compatible|compatibility|works with everything|works with more|widely used|everybody uses|industry standard|regular updates
markPoints.exemplar: It is also usually better tested and more widely compatible.

questions.example: Open source software is normally free, which matters a great deal to a charity, and because the source code is published it could be changed to suit the way the charity works. Proprietary software costs money but comes with support from the company when something goes wrong, and it is usually better tested and more compatible with what other organisations send them.
questions.paraphrase: The open option costs nothing, which suits a tight budget, and its code can be adapted to their particular needs. The paid option brings a company behind it to call when things break, along with wider compatibility and more thorough testing.
questions.feedback: Two advantages each, and they have to be advantages of THAT kind of licence. 'It is good software' applies to both.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 7 — Licence lab, station 3: Open source software

questions.q: Open source software cannot be sold.
questions.feedback: False. An open source licence is about the source code being available and modifiable, not about price. Companies do sell open source software, usually bundled with support.
questions.misconception: 'Open source means free' is the most common misconception in this topic.
